decisions.executionNote: Use left arm for left-side basket; begin smooth elbow-up lift and downward gripper orientation, approaching above eggs.
Continue left approach toward back-right basket egg, rotating to near vertical while maintaining clearance.
Visual alignment favors the front-right egg. Lower vertically with open fingers and small lateral correction.
Close around the aligned front-right egg, then begin a short vertical retention-check lift.
Lift clear of basket while keeping closed; start moving the first egg toward the left-side holder cups.
Transport visibly retained egg over the holder's back-left cup; maintain downward orientation and closed grip.
Correct held egg toward back-left cup and lower slowly; account for egg center offset from link6.
Egg is aligned in back-left cup; open to release and withdraw upward from holder/lid contact before returning toward basket.
First egg remains in back-left cup. Return over back-right basket egg with open fingers, keeping left elbow-up configuration.
Refine back-right egg alignment using wrist view; advance toward the rear of basket while descending gradually with open fingers.
Back-right egg is centered between fingers. Finish shallow descent, close fully, and lift slightly to check retention.
Fingers appear to have closed above the egg rather than around it. Reopen, shift slightly toward robot and lower before retrying.
Lift the second egg vertically to clear basket; keep closed and start toward the front-left empty holder cup.
Carry retained second egg above the empty front-left cup, avoiding the upright lid and first egg.
Lower toward front-left cup with small rightward and forward corrections for the held egg's offset from link6.
Lid contact obstructed descent. Back away toward robot and tilt the wrist to clear lid while retaining the egg, then reassess.
Recover from rejected continuity step with a forward retreat toward the preceding target configuration, then gradual tilt to clear the lid.
Use a partial orientation recovery toward the last accepted target before retreating clear of the lid; maintain grasp.
Second egg slipped onto the table in front of holder. Reopen and approach it from the robot side with a tilted wrist for recovery.
Recover the tabletop egg: descend between open fingers at the visually aligned position, then close.
Egg is still outside the fingertips. Reopen and shift the grasp toward the robot with slight clearance lift for a better centered recovery.
Egg is now between the jaws' approach paths. Make a small forward correction, close, and lift to verify recovery.
Recovered egg is visibly held. Keep it clear with left arm while bringing right arm toward the holder's right edge to reopen the prematurely closed lid.
Approach lid from its right side with right arm, keeping left-held egg well separated and both elbows up.
Align right gripper over the lid's right rim without crossing arms; keep left egg stationary.
Attempt a shallow pinch on the lid's right lip, then lift gently to reopen; watch for lid versus whole-holder motion.
Lid did not lift with pinch. Reposition closed right fingers outside the front-right corner for an under-lip lifting approach.
Slide closed right fingertips just under the lid's front-right lip and start lifting, preserving separation from the left-held egg.
Gently lift and advance the right fingertips along the lid corner to swing it open; left arm holds egg away from holder.
Previous lift missed the lip. Lower outside the front-right edge and angle fingertips inward for a lower under-lip approach.
Fingertips align at the front-right lip. Advance underneath slightly and lift along the lid-opening arc; hold the egg safely away.
Lid has started opening with the under-lip lift. Continue upward and rearward along its arc while keeping egg steady.
Push lid farther back toward its stable open position. Bring left-held egg toward front-left cup from the robot side, preserving arm separation.
Lid is open again. Withdraw right arm sideways without brushing lid; lower recovered egg toward front-left cup with left arm.
Release recovered egg into front-left cup and withdraw upward/backward. Move right arm away from holder while left returns toward remaining eggs.
Two eggs are seated in the left cups. Move left arm over the nearer remaining basket egg with open fingers; keep tilted approach to avoid lid contact later.
Center the nearer basket egg by shifting left, and descend gradually with jaws open before grasping.
Basket rim is impeding the tilted approach. Lift slightly and rotate toward vertical, moving inward to clear the rim before another descent.
Make small rightward centering correction and a shallow descent with reduced jaw spread to clear basket rim, then close around egg.
Lift the third egg vertically to verify retention and clear basket before transporting it toward the holder.
Egg stayed in basket. Reopen and return with a more vertical approach, centering over the near egg before a deeper grasp.
Egg now centered between finger paths. Narrow jaws clear of rim, close and perform a short vertical retention check.
Grasp was too high; egg stayed below closed tips. Reopen moderately and descend to egg equator before closing, avoiding basket rim.
Near egg shifted toward the basket front. Recenter the fingers slightly right and toward robot, then close and test a short lift.
Egg appears between pads. Lift vertically with closed grip and verify separation from basket before transport.
Third egg is visibly retained. Carry toward front-right cup and tilt wrist slightly toward robot to avoid the upright lid.
Approach front-right cup from the front with retained third egg, staying left of center and clear of the lid.
Correct rightward over the front-right cup and lower egg gently to seating height while keeping the wrist away from the lid.
Third egg is aligned in front-right cup. Open fully and withdraw upward toward the basket without brushing the lid.
Three eggs are visible seated. Return left arm toward the final basket egg with open jaws and a more vertical approach.
Move above the remaining rear-left basket egg, using near-vertical fingers and clearance before final descent.
Refine last egg alignment leftward and rearward while descending with sufficient jaw clearance; inspect before closing.
Last egg is between the pads. Close gently at current depth and lift vertically to verify retention before leaving basket.
Egg remained in basket after lift. Reopen and descend farther to surround its equator rather than pinching its top.
Egg is too far toward the robot relative to the jaw center. Reopen, recenter forward in the wrist view, and close around its sides.
Final egg rolled slightly forward and left. Fully reopen, shift to its new center, and lower the pads to its sides before closing.
Repeated descent is blocked by the basket rim. Lift clear and rotate the jaw direction to approach the remaining egg across its shorter axis.
With jaws rotated clear of the wall, align over the last egg and lower the pads to its sides.
Final egg lies against the right pad. Reopen slightly and center across it before closing and checking a short lift.
Closed fingertips remain above the egg. Reopen and descend farther with a small correction toward its current center before closing.
Egg is below and left of the wrist center. Back off the rim and shift diagonally toward the visible egg before closing.
Egg is centered between pads after correction. Lift vertically with closed grip to verify retention and clear the basket.
Egg slipped back into basket. Reopen and approach its new front-center location at a deeper grasp height; inspect before closure.
Make a small diagonal correction to place egg deeper between the pads, close fully, and perform a minimal lift check.
Reopen and deepen the grasp while shifting toward the egg's current front-rim location. Pause before closing to inspect pad alignment.
Egg is now at pad height. Center slightly toward the right pad, close fully and make a short straight lift to test retention.
Closed tips are still above the egg. Reopen with limited spread, descend substantially to its equator, and close without lifting yet.
The pads are forward of the egg and blocked by rim. Shift diagonally toward robot with jaws open, keeping height, then close around the exposed sides.
Rim blocks the tilted grasp. Reorient toward vertical with compensating wrist motion to keep fingertips near the egg and clear the basket wall.
Near-vertical fingers are now centered over the final egg. Lower to its sides and close without lifting until grasp alignment is checked.
At sufficient depth, shift the jaw center toward the egg's equator in the wrist view, then close and begin a minimal lift check.
Lift straight upward with closed jaws to check whether the egg is now retained; avoid sliding against the basket rim.
